newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar ends slightly firmer in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar ends slightly firmer in quiet trade.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended slightly firmer at C$1.3995 (US$0.7145) on Friday from this morning's open around C$1.4000 (US$0.7142) in moderate dealings, traders said. * They said the currency firmed on some European buying interest around midday but drifted for the rest of the day. * Investors were focused on inflation data next week.
The Canadian dollar has fallen more than two percent since the U.S. Federal Reserve raised its administered rates by 25 basis points on March 25.
Economists said the currency was hit by a small but steady selloff of Canadian dollar debt instruments due to the wider spread between short-term Canadian and U.S. yields.

The mid-point of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range for the overnight financing rate is about 250 basis points below the U.S. Federal Funds Rate and some speculated that the Fed could hike rates again next month.
The Canadian dollar continues to carry a weak bias due to pressure on the currency from the Bank of Canada's reluctance to raise Canadian rates.

Earlier this week the Bank of Canada intervened to defend the currency by buying Canadian dollars. The Bank of England also intervened on behalf of Canada's central bank during the European trading session on Thursday when the currency hit a new two-year low around C$1.4018 (US$0.7142).
Market analysts are awaiting Canada's consumer price index data for March which is scheduled to be released by Statistics Canada on Tuesday.
